questions.question: When you see a disabled pedestrian with a guide dog, white cane, or other assistive device, you must yield the right-of-way.
questions.explanation: A pedestrian with a disability using a guide dog, white cane, wheelchair, or other assistive device has the right-of-way. This applies whether they are on a sidewalk or roadway. They have the same rights as any other pedestrian.

questions.question: Seat belts work best when worn by:

options.text: All occupants every time the car is driven.

questions.correctAnswerText: All occupants every time the car is driven.
questions.explanation: Everyone in your vehicle should wear a seat belt every time you drive. In a crash, an unbelted person becomes a flying object and can injure other people in the car.

questions.question: When you encounter an aggressive driver, you should:

options.text: Avoid eye contact, slow down, and let them pass.
Cut them off to slow them down.
Make a gesture to show your disapproval.

questions.correctAnswerText: Avoid eye contact, slow down, and let them pass.
questions.explanation: If another driver is threatening you or driving dangerously near you, stay calm. Slow down and let them pass. Create distance between your vehicles. Do not make eye contact or make any gestures.

questions.question: If a flagger is directing traffic in a construction zone, you must:

options.text: Follow what other cars are doing instead of the flagger's instructions.
Assume the flagger is not supposed to be there.
Follow normal traffic laws as if the construction zone is not there.

questions.explanation: Slow down and follow directions from a flagger, sign, or law enforcement officer in a construction zone. Failing to do so is illegal and dangerous to workers.

questions.question: If an aggressive driver cuts you off, you should:

options.text: Stay calm and move away from them.
Flash your lights to show them they are wrong.
Do something aggressive back to get even.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay calm and move away from them.
questions.explanation: If an aggressive driver cuts you off, stay calm and get out of their way. Trying to get even makes the situation worse and more dangerous.

questions.question: You have a green light at an intersection, but pedestrians are crossing against the red light. You should:

options.text: Speed up and drive past the pedestrians.
Stop to let the pedestrians cross safely.
Drive close to them to scare them into not crossing against red lights.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop to let the pedestrians cross safely.
questions.explanation: Yield to pedestrians and other cars that may be in the intersection when you have a green light. Always be careful around pedestrians.

questions.question: You must stop at a railroad crossing when:

options.text: A flagger directs you to stop.
A stop sign controls the crossing.
Flashing red lights and gates are present and working.

questions.explanation: Stop at a railroad crossing when a flagger or stop sign tells you to. Also stop when flashing red lights and gates are present and operating.

questions.question: Alcohol is the number one cause of fatal car crashes.
questions.explanation: Alcohol is the top killer on American roads. Alcohol affects vision and slows reaction time, making it harder to respond to emergencies. Even small amounts of alcohol affect driving, even below the legal limit.

questions.question: Always use your turn signal when:

options.text: Pulling into or out of a parking space.
Pulling into traffic from an alley or parking area.

questions.explanation: Use your turn signal when changing lanes, pulling into or out of a parking space, or pulling into traffic from an alley or parking area. Tell other drivers what you are doing to help prevent accidents.

questions.question: A yellow and black diamond-shaped sign:

options.text: Warns you about conditions on or near the road.
Directs you to cities and towns ahead.
Tells you about traffic laws and rules.
Tells you about road construction ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Warns you about conditions on or near the road.
questions.explanation: Warning signs have black symbols or words on a yellow background and are usually diamond-shaped. They tell you about conditions on or near the road ahead.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This regulation sign tells drivers what they must do. When you see this sign, U-turns are not allowed.

questions.question: The best way to avoid hydroplaning is to:

options.text: Slow down when roads are wet or slushy.
Watch out for standing water or puddles.

questions.explanation: Wet roads cause cars to stop longer and may cause skidding on quick turns. Do not use cruise control on wet or icy roads. Reduce your speed and drive carefully.

questions.question: When changing lanes on a highway, you should:

options.text: Check your rearview and outside mirrors.
Check your blind spot by glancing over your shoulder.

questions.explanation: Before changing lanes, signal early, check your mirrors, and look over your shoulder to check your blind spot.

questions.question: Drivers who eat and drink while driving:

options.text: Are better drivers because they are not hungry.

questions.explanation: Eating, drinking, or smoking while driving is dangerous. These actions take your hands off the wheel and your eyes off the road. Drivers who do these things have trouble staying in their lanes and controlling their vehicles.

questions.question: When approaching a railroad crossing warning sign:

options.text: Be ready to drive faster than the train.
Be prepared to stop if a train is nearby.
Look for a way around any lowered gates.
Assume no trains are nearby and continue driving normally.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be prepared to stop if a train is nearby.
questions.explanation: Railroad crossing warning signs warn drivers that a train may be coming. Always obey these signs and never go around barriers.

questions.question: Before changing lanes on a multilane highway, you should:

options.text: Check your mirrors and blind spots.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check your mirrors and blind spots.
questions.explanation: Before changing lanes, look in your rearview and side mirrors to check if someone is passing you. Also look over your shoulder to check your blind spot.

questions.question: To be safe when crossing railroad tracks, you should:

options.text: Look both ways, but only when the red light is flashing.
Listen, look both ways, and then proceed if it is safe to do so.
Cross especially quickly when a train is approaching.
Quickly pass under any lowering gates.

questions.correctAnswerText: Listen, look both ways, and then proceed if it is safe to do so.
questions.explanation: Railroad crossings are always dangerous. Listen and look both ways for a train coming from either direction before crossing. Watch for warning signals and only proceed when you are sure it is safe.

questions.question: You are driving and hear a siren behind you. You should:

options.text: Pull over to the right and stop.
Speed up to get out of the way.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull over to the right and stop.
questions.explanation: When you hear a siren or see flashing lights from an emergency vehicle behind you, slow down and safely pull over to the right side of the road. If you are in heavy traffic, move slowly until you can get out of the way.

questions.question: When you see other drivers acting or reacting in anger:
questions.explanation: When other drivers are angry, distance yourself from them. Avoid making eye contact or hand gestures that could make them more upset. Slow down, move over, or do whatever you can safely do to stay away from danger.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that a flagger is ahead controlling traffic in a construction area.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. They prepare drivers for road hazards. This sign warns of a steep hill ahead. Drivers should slow down to prevent brake damage or accidents.

questions.question: You are angry after a work incident. When you get to your car, what should you do?

options.text: Play the radio loudly to stop thinking about it.
Drive fast on the highway to release stress.
Take a few minutes to calm down before driving.
Stop at a bar and drink before driving home.

questions.correctAnswerText: Take a few minutes to calm down before driving.
questions.explanation: You should always wait to calm down before driving when you are angry or upset. Driving while emotional is dangerous to yourself and others on the road.

questions.question: What can happen when you mix alcohol with another drug?

options.text: Only the alcohol effect may become weaker.

questions.explanation: Mixing alcohol with another drug can make both effects stronger. For example, one drink plus a cold medicine can affect you like several drinks.

questions.question: What should you do when driving on slippery roads?
questions.explanation: Slow down before taking curves and turns on slippery roads. This is even more important than slowing down on straight sections.

questions.question: What is the purpose of highway markings?

options.text: They are only used in construction zones.
They are red and blue in color.

questions.explanation: Highway markings help drivers. They show where to position your vehicle, mark safe passing zones, and warn about upcoming road conditions.
